options: A type of aggregate query result
A field automatically indexed by Salesforce on every object
A SOSL search scoped to a single object
A custom, narrower copy of an object containing a subset of frequently-queried fields, created by Salesforce Support to speed up reads
questions.explain: A skinny table is a narrower, Support-created copy of an object's frequently-queried fields, letting Salesforce fetch more rows per read.

questions.q: Can an org create or modify its own skinny tables directly?
options: Yes, any admin can create one from Setup
No — creating one requires contacting Salesforce Customer Support, it isn't self-service
Yes, but only through Apex metadata API calls
Skinny tables are created automatically whenever an object exceeds 1 million rows
questions.explain: Skinny tables are not self-service — they require a Salesforce Customer Support request to create or recreate.

questions.q: Per Salesforce's own guidance, when should a skinny table be requested?
options: Instead of writing selective filters, since skinny tables make selectivity irrelevant
As the very first optimization step for any slow query
Only after coding best practices and custom indexes have already been tried and found insufficient
Only for objects with fewer than 10,000 records
questions.explain: Guidance frames skinny tables as a last resort, to be requested only after other optimization techniques have already been applied and proven insufficient.

questions.q: What problem does PK chunking solve that OFFSET-based paging cannot?
options: Walking through a very large object's records in batches without hitting OFFSET's 2,000-row ceiling
Filtering records by a text search term
Aggregating records with GROUP BY
Resolving a polymorphic relationship field's type
questions.explain: PK chunking splits a Bulk API query into ID-range-bounded batches, replacing OFFSET (capped at 2,000) as the way to process a very large object's records.

questions.q: What happens to a skinny table if you change the type of a field included in it?
options: The field is automatically removed from the skinny table but the table stays valid
The skinny table automatically updates itself with no action needed
Nothing — skinny tables are unaffected by field type changes
The skinny table becomes invalid, and Support must create a new one
questions.explain: Altering a field's type that's part of a skinny table invalidates it; a new skinny table has to be requested from Support.
